DEFAULT.title: DEFAULT · Warm Contemporary
DEFAULT.tagline: Bed faces the balcony, wardrobe fills the alcove, study-dresser on the thick wall.
DEFAULT.why: It uses every piece of the L-shaped room for what it is best at. The 5'4" x 3'4" alcove beside the door is exactly the size of a 3-door wardrobe, so storage costs no floor space. The bed sits on the only long solid wall (east) and faces the 10'5" balcony opening, giving the best view and morning light. The 7'3" thick south wall becomes a study-cum-dresser. That leaves a clear 5'8" zone between the bed and the balcony and a 3'10" walkway from the door. Aluminium sliders, laminate and vitrified tile are standard, affordable and low-maintenance in Indian conditions.

OPTION_D.title: Option D · Smart Budget (Indian)
OPTION_D.tagline: The same well-planned layout as DEFAULT for about ₹1,93,300: ready-made pieces, a local carpenter and colour instead of costly finishes.
OPTION_D.why: Money goes where it lasts and gets used every day: a full-height wardrobe with a loft, proper aluminium sliders for the balcony and the window, and a good mattress. It saves on things that cost a lot but add little: no false ceiling, no panelling, no veneer or acrylic, and the existing floor stays. The look comes from colour and Indian textiles: a terracotta accent wall, indigo cotton curtains, a handloom dhurrie, a cane moodha and a Madhubani print. Walnut and frosty-white laminate tie the carpenter work to the ready-made bed. The layout is DEFAULT's, which already works: bed facing the balcony, wardrobe in the alcove, study-dresser on the thick wall.

OPTION_E.title: Option E · Simple & Practical
OPTION_E.tagline: About ₹1,47,900 as recommended (₹1,28,400 with the 'Within ₹1.3 lakh' pick): plain paint, a sliding wardrobe with the mirror on its door, a standing desk. ✏️ Customise changes the 3D, colours and budget.
OPTION_E.why: This is how an interior designer keeps a small bedroom on a budget: spend on what you use every day (a good wardrobe, bed, mattress, a proper desk, a fan and good light) and skip what only looks fancy. The walls are simply painted: one washable paint, two shades. Nothing hangs from the ceiling except the fan and lights, the builder's windows stay, and no furniture stands in a walkway. Unlike DEFAULT there is no lounge chair: this room has no free spot where a chair can be used without blocking the path beside the bed. You sit at the desk, on the bed, or later on the balcony.

sections.Layout: Bed centred on the east wall (the only long solid wall), facing the balcony. One bedside on the window side and a floating shelf on the door side, so both walkways stay about 2'2" wide. Standing desk and a pegboard on the thick wall. Sliding wardrobe with the full-length mirror on its door, right by the room's entrance. Fan over the foot of the bed. 5' of open floor between the bed and the balcony door.
sections.Wardrobe & mirror: Sliding doors, because the wardrobe sits right at the room's entrance: hinged doors would swing into your path. The mirror goes on the front sliding door, so you dress where your clothes are and it throws balcony light into the alcove. The wall that had the mirror becomes a pegboard for your bag, headphones and keys. Prefer to see the whole wardrobe at once? Choose hinged doors in ✏️ Customise.
sections.Ceiling (bare concrete now): Your ceiling is the underside of the RCC roof slab. It needs: ~12 mm gypsum plaster (punning) to make it smooth → putty → primer → 2 coats ceiling-white paint. Before plastering, fix the fan hook (anchor fastener rated for a fan) and run the light wires in thin surface conduits, because RCC can't be cut for pipes. If the flat has a terrace above, get the roof waterproofed and coated with heat-reflective white paint first.
sections.Walls & paint: One washable emulsion everywhere (Asian Paints Apcolite Premium or a Berger / Nerolac equivalent, matt or low-sheen). Warm off-white on three walls, pale sage on the bed wall, ceiling white. Process: fill cracks → sand → primer on the patches → 2 coats. If the walls are still grey cement, they need 2 full coats of putty first (choose 'Bare cement plaster' in ✏️ Customise).
sections.Lighting & fan: 1200 mm BLDC fan (~30 W, with remote). 4 surface LED panels (4000K) placed away from the pillows, 2 warm wall reading lights, a 20 W LED batten under the desk shelf. AC point and pipe sleeve done now for a split AC later.
sections.Standing desk: Single-motor electric sit-stand desk, 4'×2', with memory presets. Set the standing height so your elbows are at 90° (about 3'5" for someone 5'6"–5'8"); sitting height about 2'4". Monitor top at eye level. Anti-fatigue mat; the mesh chair tucks under when you stand.
sections.Window & door: The builder's aluminium sliders are kept (clean the tracks, oil the rollers). A pleated mosquito mesh is added to the balcony door. Beige blackout eyelet curtains on plain SS rods. Upgrade W1 to a uPVC tilt-and-turn window in ✏️ Customise if you want quieter, dust-tight, rain-safe ventilation.
sections.Palette: Warm off-white, pale sage, light oak, white, beige, denim blue. Change any of them in ✏️ Customise.
